block.txt: An Act to establish and confer functions on Museums of History NSW and repeal the Historic Houses Act 1980; to amend the State Records Act 1998 to transfer certain functions of the State Archives and Records Authority of New South Wales to Museums of History NSW and consequently rename the Authority; and for other purposes.
This Act is the Museums of History NSW Act 2022.
This Act commences as follows—
for Schedule 4[1], [3], [17] and [21]–[25]—on 1 January 2024,
otherwise—on 31 December 2022.
In this Act—
acquire includes purchase or lease.
advisory committee means an advisory committee established under Schedule 1, section 7.
Board means the Board of Museums of History NSW.
building includes—
part of a building, and
a structure or part of a structure, and
associated grounds or works.
Chief Executive Officer means the person employed in the Public Service under the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 as the Chief Executive Officer of Museums of History NSW.
control, of a State record, has the same meaning as in the State Records Act 1998.
exercise a function includes perform a duty.
function includes the following—
power,
authority,
duty.
gift includes the following—
devise,
bequest.
member means a member of the Board appointed under section 7.
record has the same meaning as in the State Records Act 1998.
significant building or site—see section 13.
site includes associated works.
State archive means a State record that Museums of History NSW has control of under the State Records Act 1998.
State record has the same meaning as in the State Records Act 1998.
written notice includes electronic communication.
The Interpretation Act 1987 contains definitions and other provisions that affect the interpretation and application of this Act.
This Act does not—
affect the operation of the Heritage Act 1977, or
apply to land reserved under the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.

heading.b: Constitution and management of Museums of History NSW
Constitution of Museums of History NSW

block.txt: There is constituted by this Act a body corporate with the corporate name of Museums of History NSW.

heading.b: Status of Museums of History NSW

block.txt: Museums of History NSW is a statutory body representing the Crown.
See the Interpretation Act 1987, section 13A.
Museums of History NSW is subject to the control and direction of the Minister in the exercise of its functions.

heading.b: Board of Museums of History NSW

block.txt: There is a Board of Museums of History NSW.
The general policies and strategic direction of Museums of History NSW is to be decided by the Board.
The Board consists of 12 members appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Minister.
The appointed members must include the following—
at least 1 person who has knowledge of, or experience in, history or the archival profession,
at least 1 person who has knowledge of, or experience in, heritage,
at least 1 person who has knowledge of, or experience in, First Nations cultures,
at least one young person.
The Minister must appoint—
1 of the appointed members as the Chairperson of the Board, and
1 of the appointed members as the Deputy Chairperson of the Board.
Schedule 1 contains provisions relating to the constitution and procedure of the Board.
In this section—
young person means a person who, at the time of appointment as a member, is—
at least 18 years of age, and
not more than 28 years of age.
The Minister must consult the Board before appointing a person to the office of Chief Executive Officer.
The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the day-to-day management of the affairs of Museums of History NSW.
The Chief Executive Officer must exercise the Chief Executive Officer’s functions in accordance with the general directions, including policies, of the Board.
Anything done on behalf of Museums of History NSW by, or with the authority of, the Chief Executive Officer is taken to have been done by Museums of History NSW.
The Chief Executive Officer may participate in meetings of the Board, but is not entitled to vote at the meetings.
Persons may be employed in the Public Service under the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 to enable Museums of History NSW to exercise its functions.

The Government Sector Employment Act 2013, section 59 provides that the persons employed, or whose services Museums of History NSW makes use of, may be referred to as officers or employees, or members of staff, of Museums of History NSW. The Constitution Act 1902, section 47A precludes Museums of History NSW from employing staff.

heading.b: Objects and functions of Museums of History NSW
Objects of Museums of History NSW

block.txt: The main objects of Museums of History NSW are as follows—
to collect, manage and preserve the following (the collection)—
State archives,
significant buildings and sites,
objects and materials related to significant buildings and sites,
to increase—
public knowledge and enjoyment of the collection, and
access to the collection,
to promote—
knowledge and appreciation of history, and
the stories that shape the social, historical, political and cultural identity of New South Wales,
to achieve the objects described in paragraphs (a)–(c) across the State, including in regional and rural New South Wales.

heading.b: Functions of Museums of History NSW

block.txt: Museums of History NSW has the following functions—
to acquire, control and manage significant buildings and sites,
certain functions under the State Records Act 1998,
functions conferred on it by this Act or another Act or law,
functions supplementary or incidental to the exercise of its other functions, including the following—
entering contracts or arrangements,
charging fees for goods or services, including permissions given,
applying for licences, permits or other authorities,
anything prescribed by the regulations.
A fee received under subsection (1)(d)(ii) is to be kept for use by Museums of History NSW.
Museums of History NSW may delegate the exercise of a function, other than this power of delegation, to the following—
a member of the Board,
an advisory committee,
the Chief Executive Officer,
a member of staff of Museums of History NSW.

In this Act, a significant building or site means a building or site that, in the opinion of Museums of History NSW, holds architectural, social, historical, cultural or political significance for the history or identity of the State.

heading.b: Powers related to significant buildings and sites

block.txt: Museums of History NSW may do the following in pursuing its objects—
acquire a building or site for—
exhibition, or
restoration, or
maintenance, or
another purpose approved by the Minister,
lend property in circumstances Museums of History NSW thinks fit,
permit members of the public to enter a significant building or site under its control or management,
permit the use of a significant building or site under its control or management for the following if, in the opinion of Museums of History NSW, it is appropriate for the building or site—
a conference or meeting,
an educational, cultural or other activity,
a function or event,
photography or as a set for audio or video production,
the provision of food or beverages by Museums of History NSW or another person,
promote or provide educational services, including exhibitions, lectures and films,
engage the services of and pay fees to persons including—
consultants or photographers, or
artists, entertainers, lecturers or performers engaged to appear at a significant building or site under its control or management.
Museums of History NSW may agree to a condition being imposed in relation to the acquisition of property if the condition is not inconsistent with its objects.
The rule of law against remoteness of vesting does not apply to the condition.
Museums of History NSW may impose conditions in relation to the admission of the public to, or the use of, a significant building or site under its control or management.

Museums of History NSW may conduct reasonable investigations for the purpose of deciding if a building or site is suitable for control and management by Museums of History NSW as a significant building or site.
The Minister may, by written notice given to Museums of History NSW, impose conditions on the conduct of investigations under this section.
Museums of History NSW must comply with the conditions in relation to the investigation.

heading.b: Acquisition of significant buildings and sites

block.txt: The Minister may authorise Museums of History NSW to acquire a building or site.
The authorisation must be given by written notice.
The Minister may give the authorisation only if satisfied that the building or site is suitable for control and management by Museums of History NSW as a significant building or site.
Museums of History NSW may acquire the building or site in accordance with the authorisation.

heading.b: Acquisition of significant building or site vested in public authority

block.txt: The Governor may, by order published in the Gazette, declare that land vested in a public authority is divested from the public authority and vested in Museums of History NSW for the estate or interest specified in the order.
The Governor may make the order if requested by the Minister.
The Minister may request the Governor to make the order if—
the Minister has consulted the public authority, and
is satisfied the land is suitable for control and management by Museums of History NSW as a significant building or site.
On publication of the order in the Gazette—
a dedication described in the order in relation to the land is revoked, and
the land is vested in Museums of History NSW for the estate or interest specified in the order, and
the land is discharged from all trusts affecting the land immediately before publication, other than a trust specified in the order as not being discharged, and
personal property of the public authority, including all rights and interests in the property, is vested in Museums of History NSW if the property—
immediately before publication, was used by the authority in connection with the land, and
is specified in the order, and
an agreement or undertaking entered into by the public authority in connection with the land is taken to be entered into by Museums of History NSW, and
a security or charge over the land is taken to have been given by Museums of History NSW, and

a condition subject to which the public authority acquired personal property or a right or interest in personal property by gift is taken to be agreed to by Museums of History NSW under section 14(2).
A dispute between a public authority and Museums of History NSW about an order under this section must be resolved by the Premier.
In this section—
dedication includes a reservation or other setting apart of land.
public authority means—
the Crown, or
a Minister of the Crown, or
a statutory body representing the Crown, or
a constructing authority under the Public Works and Procurement Act 1912 or another Act that provides for the application of provisions of that Act.

heading.b: Restoration or alteration of significant buildings and sites

block.txt: Museums of History NSW may carry out, or arrange for the carrying out of, in relation to a significant building or site under its control or management—
restoration works, or
alterations or improvements.
The Minister may, by written notice given to Museums of History NSW, impose conditions on restoration works carried out under this section.
Museums of History NSW must ensure the restoration works are carried out in accordance with the conditions.
Museums of History NSW may make conservation management plans that apply to 1 or more significant buildings or sites under its control or management.
A conservation management plan must be approved by the Board.
Museums of History NSW must ensure alterations or improvements are carried out in accordance with a conservation management plan that applies to the significant building or site.
Museums of History NSW must not dispose of property, except—
for real property acquired without conditions—with the approval of the Governor, or
for other property acquired without conditions—with the approval of the Minister, or
for property acquired subject to a condition—
in accordance with the condition, or
in accordance with subsection (3).
An approval of the Governor or Minister may be given in relation to particular property or a class of property.
Museums of History NSW may dispose of property acquired subject to a condition other than in accordance with the condition if—
it resolves that the property is no longer required for its purposes, and
the Governor approves the disposal, and
the disposal is carried out in accordance with any conditions imposed by the Governor as part of the Governor’s approval.
Museums of History NSW may dispose of property under subsection (3) by—
selling the property and keeping for its use the proceeds of the sale, or
exchanging the property for other property, or
giving the property to an organisation whose rules or objects require its resources to be used wholly or predominantly for the promotion of education in Australia, or
if Museums of History NSW is of the opinion that the property is of no commercial value—disposing of the property otherwise than for valuable consideration.
In this section—
condition means a condition to which Museums of History NSW has agreed under section 14(2).
dispose includes sell, mortgage or lease for a term of more than 6 months.
Museums of History NSW may acquire property—
to be the offices of Museums of History NSW, or
to be residential accommodation for the caretaker of a significant building or site under its control or management, or
for another purpose reasonably necessary for, or incidental to, the exercise of the functions of Museums of History NSW.
The Minister may, by written notice given to Museums of History NSW, impose conditions on the acquisition of property under this section.
Museums of History NSW must comply with the conditions in relation to the acquisition.
Museums of History NSW must not dispose of the fee simple estate in Throsby Park Historic Site, unless specifically authorised by an Act of Parliament.
Museums of History NSW may, subject to conditions it thinks fit—
lease Throsby Park Historic Site, or
dispose of an interest, other than the fee simple, in Throsby Park Historic Site, or
create an estate or interest in Throsby Park Historic Site.
A lease or licence granted under this section must not have a term that, together with the term of a further lease or licence that may be granted under an option, is more than 99 years.
In this section—
Throsby Park Historic Site means the following land at Moss Vale—
Lot K, Filed Plan 109154,
The Duties Act 1997 does not apply in relation to—
a gift made, or to be made, to Museums of History NSW, or
the transfer of assets, rights or liabilities under section 17.

heading.b: Functions related to State archives and records

block.txt: Museums of History NSW has functions under the State Records Act 1998, including functions relating to the following—
records management services,
assuming control of State records that are not currently in use,
recovering estrays and other State records,
facilitating public access to State records,
copying and publishing State archives,
exercising a right of the Crown as the owner of copyright subsisting in a State archive.
In this section—
estrays has the same meaning as in the State Records Act 1998.
A protected person is not personally subject to liability for anything done or omitted to be done—
in good faith, and
for the purpose of exercising a function under this Act.
The liability attaches to the Crown instead.
In this section—
liability—
means civil liability, and
includes an action, claim or demand.
protected person means—
a member of the Board, or
a member of an advisory committee, or
the Chief Executive Officer, or
a person acting under the direction of 1 of the following—
Museums of History NSW,
the Board,
an advisory committee,
the Chief Executive Officer.
The Governor may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, about a matter that is—
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed, or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may provide for matters relating to the following—
the constitution or procedures of the Board,
advisory committees,
the use of a significant building or site or other property of Museums of History NSW,
services provided by Museums of History NSW,
the parking or movement of vehicles on land controlled or managed by Museums of History NSW.
The regulations may create offences punishable by a maximum penalty of 5 penalty units.
Proceedings for an offence under the regulations are to be dealt with summarily before the Local Court.
section 7
In this Schedule—
Chairperson means the Chairperson of the Board.
committee member means a member of an advisory committee.
Deputy Chairperson means the Deputy Chairperson of the Board.
A member holds office for the period of not more than 3 years specified in the member’s instrument of appointment.
A member is eligible, if otherwise qualified, for reappointment.
A member must not hold office for more than 3 consecutive terms.

For the purposes of calculating the number of consecutive terms of office that a member has held, an appointment to fill a vacancy for the balance of a member’s term of office must not be taken into account.
Members, acting members and committee members are entitled to be paid remuneration, including travelling and subsistence allowances, as determined by the Minister from time to time.
In this section—
acting member means a person appointed to act as a member under this Schedule, section 4.
committee member means a member of an advisory committee who is not also a member of the Board.
The Minister may, from time to time, appoint a person to act in the office of a member during—
the member’s absence, or
a vacancy in the office of the member, until a person is appointed by the Governor to fill the vacancy.
The person, while acting—
is taken to be a member, and
has all the functions of the member.
The Minister may revoke an appointment made under this section at any time.
This section does not operate to confer on a person acting in the office of a member who is the Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson the member’s functions as Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson.
The office of a member becomes vacant if the member—
dies, or
completes a term of office and is not reappointed, or
resigns from office by written notice addressed to the Minister, or
is removed from office by the Minister under this section, or
is absent from 3 consecutive meetings of the Board of which reasonable notice has been given to the member personally or by post, unless—
the member is on leave granted by the Board, or
within 6 weeks of the third meeting, the member is excused by the Board for having been absent from the meetings, or

becomes bankrupt, applies to take the benefit of a law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors, compounds with the member’s creditors or makes an assignment of the member’s remuneration for the benefit of the member’s creditors, or
becomes a mentally incapacitated person, or
is convicted in New South Wales of, or convicted elsewhere of an offence that, if committed in New South Wales, would be, an offence that is punishable by imprisonment for 12 months or more.
The Minister may remove a member from office at any time.
If the office of a member becomes vacant, a person must be appointed to fill the vacancy.
A member vacates office as Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson if the member—
ceases to be a member, or
resigns from the office by written notice addressed to the Minister, or
is removed from the office by the Minister under this section.
The Minister may remove a member from office as Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson at any time.
If the office of Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson becomes vacant, a member must be appointed to fill the vacancy.

For the purposes of subsection (1)(a), a member does not cease to be a member on the expiry of the member’s term of office if the member is reappointed as a member for a term commencing immediately after the expiration of the previous term.
The Board may establish 1 or more advisory committees to assist the Board in the exercise of the Board’s functions.
The Board must prepare and approve an advisory committee charter that provides for—
the appointment of committee members, and
the functions and responsibilities of advisory committees, and
other relevant matters.
The Board must appoint committee members in accordance with the advisory committee charter.
At least 1 person appointed to the committee must also be a member of the Board.
This Schedule, sections 11, 13 and 14 apply to advisory committees and committee members in the same way the sections apply to the Board and members.
The provisions of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 relating to the employment of Public Service employees do not apply to a member.

A provision of another Act does not disqualify a person from holding a specified office and also the office of a member, or from accepting and retaining remuneration payable to the person under this Part, section 3, merely because the provision—
requires a person who is the holder of the specified office to devote the whole of the person’s time to the duties of the office, or
prohibits the person from engaging in employment outside the duties of the office.
The procedure for calling a meeting of the Board and for conducting business at meetings is, subject to this Act and the regulations, to be as determined by the Board.
The Minister may call the first meeting of the Board in the way the Minister thinks fit.
The quorum for a meeting of the Board is a majority of members for the time being.
The Chairperson must preside at a meeting of the Board, unless the Chairperson is absent.
If the Chairperson is absent—
the Deputy Chairperson must preside, or
if the Deputy Chairperson is absent—1 of the members present at the meeting, as elected by the other members present, must preside.
The person presiding at a meeting has—
a deliberative vote, and
in the event of an equality of votes—a second or casting vote.
A decision supported by a majority of the votes cast at a meeting of the Board at which a quorum is present is the decision of the Board.
The Board must keep full and accurate minutes of the proceedings of each meeting of the Board.
A member must disclose the nature of a pecuniary interest at a meeting of the Board as soon as possible after the relevant facts have come to the member’s knowledge.
A member has a pecuniary interest if—
the member has a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in a matter being considered, or about to be considered, at a meeting of the Board, and
the interest appears to raise a conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties in relation to the consideration of the matter.

A disclosure is a sufficient disclosure of the nature of an interest in a matter relating to a corporation or other body, or to a person, which may arise after the date of the disclosure and which is required to be disclosed under subsection (1), if the disclosure is that the member—
is a member of, or employed by, a specified corporation or other body, or
is a partner of, or employed by, a specified person, or
has another interest relating to a specified corporation or other body, or to a specified person.
Particulars of a disclosure made under this section must be recorded by the Board in a book that is—
kept for the purpose of recording disclosures, and
open to inspection at all reasonable hours by a person on payment of the fee determined by the Board.
After a member has disclosed the nature of an interest in a matter, the member must not, unless the Board otherwise determines—
be present during a deliberation of the Board about the matter, or
take part in a decision of the Board about the matter.
For the purposes of the making of a determination under subsection (5), a member who has a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in a matter to which the disclosure relates must not—
be present during a deliberation of the Board for the purpose of making the determination, or
take part in the making of the determination.
A contravention of this section does not invalidate a decision of the Board.
This section applies to a committee member and the advisory committee in the same way it applies to a member and the Board.

heading.b: Transaction of business outside meetings or by telephone or other means

block.txt: The Board may transact its business by the circulation of papers, including by electronic means, among all members for the time being.

If the Board transacts business by the circulation of papers, a written resolution, approved in writing by a majority of members, is taken to be a decision of the Board made at a meeting of the Board.

The Board may transact its business at a meeting at which 1 or more members participate by telephone or other electronic means, provided a member who speaks on a matter can be heard by the other members.
The Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson and each other member have the same voting rights as they would have at an ordinary meeting of the Board for the purposes of—
the approval of a resolution under subsection (2), or
a meeting held in accordance with subsection (3).
A resolution approved under subsection (2) must be recorded in the minutes of the meetings of the Board.
The regulations may contain provisions of a savings or transitional nature consequent on the commencement of—
a provision of this Act, or
a provision amending this Act.
A savings or transitional provision consequent on the commencement of a provision must not be made more than 2 years after that commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision is repealed 2 years after that commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision may take effect before that commencement but not before—
for a provision of this Act—the date of assent to this Act, or
for a provision amending this Act—the date of assent to the amending Act.
A savings or transitional provision taking effect before its publication on the NSW legislation website does not, before its publication—
affect the rights of a person in a way prejudicial to the person, or
impose liabilities on a person for anything done or omitted to be done.
In this section—
person does not include—
the State, or
an authority of the State.

heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of this Act

block.txt: In this Part—
assets means the assets vested in, or otherwise held by, both of the following immediately before the commencement day—
the Trust,
the former trustees on behalf of the Trust.
commencement day means the day on which this Part commences.
former trustees means the trustees of the Trust appointed under the repealed Act, section 6.
liabilities means the liabilities of the Trust, including liabilities enforceable against a former trustee in their capacity as trustee, immediately before the commencement day.
repealed Act means the Historic Houses Act 1980 as in force before the commencement day.
rights means the rights of the Trust, including rights enforceable by a former trustee in their capacity as trustee, immediately before the commencement day.
Trust means the Historic Houses Trust of New South Wales established under the repealed Act.
The Trust is dissolved.

The persons who were trustees of the Trust immediately before the Trust’s dissolution cease to be trustees, but are eligible, if otherwise qualified, to be appointed as members of the Board of Museums of History NSW.
No compensation is payable for a loss of office under this section.

heading.b: References to Trust and former trustees

block.txt: A reference in the following to the Trust or the former trustees is to be read as a reference to Museums of History NSW—
another Act or law,
an instrument related to a gift that would have vested in the Trust had this Act not commenced,
a document.

heading.b: Vesting of assets, liabilities and rights

block.txt: On and from the commencement day—
the assets vest in Museums of History NSW without the need for a further conveyance, transfer, assignment or assurance, and
the liabilities and rights become the liabilities and rights of Museums of History NSW, and

all proceedings relating to the assets, liabilities or rights commenced by or against the former trustees and pending before the commencement day are taken to be pending proceedings by or against Museums of History NSW, and

an act, matter or thing done or not done by, to or for the Trust in relation to the assets, liabilities or rights before the commencement day is taken to have been done or not done by, to or for Museums of History NSW, and

Museums of History NSW has the entitlements and obligations, whether actual or potential, of the Trust and the former trustees in relation to the assets, liabilities and rights that the Trust and the former trustees would have had if the Trust had not been dissolved, and
Museums of History NSW is deemed to have agreed under this Act, section 14(2) to each condition subject to which the Trust acquired property or a right or interest.
No assignment of a lease is required as a result of this section.
The operation of this section is not to be regarded as—
a breach of contract or confidence or otherwise as a civil wrong, or
a breach of a contractual provision prohibiting, restricting or regulating the assignment or transfer of an asset, liability or right, or
an event of default under a contract or other instrument, or

giving rise to a remedy by a party to an instrument, or as causing or permitting the termination of an instrument, because of a change in the beneficial or legal ownership of an asset, liability or right.

heading.b: Appointment of first Chief Executive Officer

block.txt: Despite this Act, section 8, the Minister may appoint the first person to office as Chief Executive Officer without consulting the Board if all of the members of the Board have not been appointed.

heading.b: Provision consequent on enactment of Museums of History NSW Amendment (Chief Executive Officer) Act 2024

block.txt: The person holding office as the Chief Executive Officer immediately before the commencement of the amending Act continues in office for the balance of the term of office specified in the person’s instrument of appointment, unless the person vacates or is removed from office sooner.

This Act, as in force immediately before the commencement of the amending Act, continues to apply in relation to the appointment until a subsequent appointment is made after the commencement of the amending Act.
In this section—
amending Act means the Museums of History NSW Amendment (Chief Executive Officer) Act 2024.
